label: Meaningfulness closed under negation: MeaningClosedUnderNegation L meaningful: for every sentence…
term: meaningfulness closed under negation (strong and weak)
definition: `MeaningClosedUnderNegation L meaningful` (strong): for every sentence s, if s is meaningful then its negation is meaningful. `MeaningClosedUnderNegationOfNegations L meaningful` (weak): for every s, if the negation of s is meaningful then its double negation is. `meaningful` is the pre-theoretic predicate (sense (2) of DISAMB-VERIFICATIONIST-MEANINGFUL), not a criterion's verdict.
note: Owner-approved floor items (2026-11-05, #1008), strong and weak siblings (#1017). Hempel's adequacy assumption, as SEP reports it, is the biconditional; both versions are parts of its left-to-right half.
